items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: I learned that from Clark Terry. I learned that from one of the great music educators out there whose name ... you may or may not know, Paul Effman.

ctx.x: So it’s a very, very, very deep point that over time, and this is one of the blessings about getting older, after a while you try things, they work, they don’t work, you bomb, and you get the kids. Another thing like that is I don’t primarily like to teach from the method books, okay? Now every student at some point in time when they’re in the school they’re going to get the Belwin Band Builder or the this or what-have-you. So there are concepts that I embellish or I take from the Belwin Band Builder let’s call…

you may or may not know, Paul Effman. Okay? Paul, a music educator, came up with a model to have schools in — have music programs in private and parochial schools and eventually it developed into something like seven or eight hundred schools. But the idea was it’s entertaining and educational and motivating and something that you will always try to remember.
